The prompts when run-time capture was built; the version the weekly batch starts on unless a prompt changes first.
Only the tax rules reference document changed (treaty article, superficial-loss window, RRSP withdrawal and TFSA rules). No agent reads it since the Tax Strategist was removed, so no call can move.

The price band is centred on a stock-specific baseline (the stock's required return plus the edge its fundamentals and estimate revisions give, from the latest weekly fit over the reference universe) instead of the flat risk-free rate plus 4% for every stock; stocks that cannot be valued keep the flat centre. The prompts and the CIO's call are unchanged (the CIO does not see the baseline until the tier is redefined against it).

The valuation baseline is shown to Bull, Bear, the CIO and the Shadow CIO as one code-built block, so valuation enters the debate once. The CIO's tier is read against the baseline's expected return (it was an absolute return); the advocates may cite BASELINE and the CIO may name it as a decision factor's source. The band's cold-start reference is 0.0 (it was 0.46, the mean of absolute-tier readings), and only readings from runs of this version or later enter the view history, the cross-stock reference and the optimizer's jump rule. The view is still the four-week average and the advocates' conviction tables are still definition 4 (both change in P17).

The Stock Researcher no longer gets peer blocks (the two companies nearest in market cap) and no longer writes competitive_position or peer_comparison_summary; Bull, Bear, Risk and the CIO no longer read those two fields, and a missing peer block no longer counts as a data gap, so about 7% of Researcher data-quality readings move from medium to high. The CIO's and the advocates' own prompts, the band settings and the model are unchanged.

The Macro, Fundamental and Researcher agents are shown a code-built block of the company's own numbers from its annual accounts (rate, inflation and currency exposure for Macro; margins, return on capital and cost share for the other two), and their prompts name it as a citation source. The Macro payload carries the broad US dollar index beside CAD/USD, one fixed currency hint replaces the per-country ones, and a sentence that contradicts the payload's rate or inflation label, or a margin or return direction the block computed, is retried (soft errors). Fundamental must state the block's operating margin and return on capital direction, the Researcher keeps the filing's ROIC apart from the computed one, a company whose currency line shows no exposure gets a neutral currency impact, the Technology rate hint no longer reads as a benefit of tightening, mid_cycle is ruled out under a tightening rate or rising CPI, and Bull, Bear and the Risk Advisor read the block's multi-year history in the Fundamental view. Pass 2 reads the currency label that matches the company's reporting currency. SP_COMPANY_FACTS=0 switches the blocks off. A Pass 1 narrative within 10 percent over its length limit is no longer retried, one up to 60 percent over is retried with a character target and then accepted, and only a longer one fails (branch pass1-narrative-tolerance). The CIO's and the advocates' own prompts, the band settings and the model are unchanged.

The Macro agent's currency and pricing claims are checked in code: a sentence that states a currency move as an effect on earnings, profit or margins, or says anything about pricing power, is retried (soft errors; the block shows revenue translation only and no figure shows pricing power), and when the currency line says whether the company hedges is unknown and the currency impact is not neutral, the rationale gets one fixed sentence saying so (code, no retry). The Macro prompt is told to state the current direction from the blocks' new latest-year note and to give the period word only with its years, and its inflation step asks about input costs only, no longer about pricing power, so the prompt no longer invites the claim the check flags. The Fundamental and Researcher prompts are unchanged. The blocks themselves print a note, for example ', but latest year falling (-1.2 points)', when the last fiscal year moved against the first-to-last direction word (code, no prompt). The CIO's and the advocates' own prompts, the band settings and the model are unchanged.

The business profile (ClickUp 86bctjbfk) reaches the Macro and Researcher agents as code-built lines inside the company blocks they already read, cited COMPANY like the rest of the block, with no new citation token. The Macro COMPANY EXPOSURE block carries 12-month readings under the channel each belongs to: inputs (the inputs the filing names first, then the archetype table's expected inputs labelled as not confirmed by a filing, each with its BEA cost share), labor beside the company's own revenue per employee, the price the company sells at, freight, trade beside the China share of revenue where the filing tags one, and the Canadian dollar for a Canadian company. The Researcher company block carries the model's labels marked unchecked and the table's demand readings with the company's own sensitivity stated as not measured. The Macro prompt's COMPANY EXPOSURE rule and inflation step say how to read them (quote the window, the block's own word, no effect on earnings the block does not state); the Researcher's first step asks what moves demand. A Macro pass2 view key, industry_readings, carries the readings to Bull, Bear and the Risk Advisor (code). A soft-error check retries a sentence that contradicts a reading's direction, quotes it without its 12-month window, or states an effect on earnings (code). The Fundamental analyst's, the advocates' and the CIO's prompts, the band settings and the model are unchanged. The lines appear when the bundle holds a shown profile; the profile is built on every analysis (the switch SP_BUSINESS_PROFILE was removed, ticket step 4), so a stock in a shown industry gets them.

Two small corrections found by the first real runs after the configuration work. The Macro agent's data quality no longer counts a high VIX or an inverted yield curve as an anomaly: they are true readings of the market, still shown to the model in its warnings line in the same order, but they no longer set the agent's data quality to low, no longer demand a caveat (16 of 51 Macro runs since 2026-11-10 were retried for it) and no longer show Pass 2 a MACRO quality of low; a stale series or a data anomaly (an unusually large move) still does. The Sentiment prompt's Canadian caveat rule now says it applies only when the data names a Canadian stock, instead of printing the flag as 'if false is true'. Checked on stored bundles: Sentiment passed its first attempt on two Canadian and two US stocks; a wider Macro prompt rewording to cut the other three rejections (a 12-month window on a COMPANY figure, 'neutral rates' against a tightening payload, a currency impact against a no-exposure line) was measured on 12 stored bundles and not adopted (22 attempts before, 21 and 25 after: the errors moved, they did not fall).

data.description: One sentence added to the hard constraints of the Bull, Bear and Risk Advisor prompts: the stated ranges are limits to stay inside, not targets, and a narrative over its cap or a list over its count is rejected and written again. Found on the first Haiku runs, where Pass 2 overshot a length cap (a Bull narrative of 3,325 characters against 3,300, eight caveats against five, a Risk narrative of 2,680 against 2,400) and each overshoot cost a retry. The wording changes no range and no rule; its effect on gpt-oss is not measured. Alongside it the Bear thesis-invalidator check stopped flagging negated or cost-side phrases as bad events (non-dilutive funding, without heavy dilution, a cut in burn) and the profile-reading check stopped reading a second series' name as an earnings claim, both false flags seen on Haiku runs; neither changes a prompt.
